name: jarvis-cloud
description: Use Jarvis from my phone without leaving my PC running.

paragraphs: Use Jarvis from my phone without leaving my PC running.

This repository is for a separate cloud deployment of Hermes Agent, connected to the Jarvis web interface. Keeping it separate means the local setup remains available if cloud hosting stops working. Computer access, local Ollama models and heavier rendering stay on the PC.

The service runs Hermes's native API gateway in Docker. The initial cloud profile uses OpenRouter's free pool, which runs out after 50 requests a day. Two optional fallbacks pick up after it, in this order: NVIDIA, then Google Gemini (GEMINIAPIKEY, model gemini-2.5-flash unless GEMINIMODEL says otherwise). Gemini runs through Hermes's built-in Gemini provider, which adapts tool definitions for Google; its free tier is small (a few hundred requests a day), so it stretches a conversation rather than replacing the other two. Groq is left out on purpose: its free tier caps tokens per minute below…

whatItDoes.text: Use Jarvis from my phone without leaving my PC running.

requirements.text: A web frontend should keep that key server-side behind its own sign-in flow.

Global Hermes memory, user profiles, cross-session searches, server file access and terminal execution are disabled: the shared runtime does not provide a separate filesystem or memory store for every account.
